proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary represented model \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\) and assignments \(x\), \(c\), and \(y\) in the finite support spaces declared in the target.  For every \(A\subseteq V\), put
\[
 \mathcal X_A(\mathbf M)
 :=\prod_{v\in A}\operatorname{supp}_{\mathbf M}(V_v),
\]
with \(\mathcal X_{\varnothing}(\mathbf M)\) equal to the singleton containing the empty assignment.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\) makes the assignment \(a\in\mathcal X_W(\mathbf M)\), defined by \(a_X=x\) and \(a_C=c\), well defined.  At a role state \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\), write \(\bar x=a_{\bar X}\) and \(\bar c=a_{\bar C}\), and define the proof-local conditional kernel
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 :=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),
 \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\right).
 \tag{1}
\]
The sets in (1) are pairwise compatible: the definition of a role state gives \(\bar X\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar C=W=X\cup C\), while \(Y\cap W=\varnothing\) follows from \(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}discrete\text{-}selected\text{-}model}\), the finite selected stratum used in (1) has positive mass at every assignment under consideration; explicitly,
\[
 P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1
 \mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x)\right)>0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus every conditional probability and every division below is defined, including the boundary case \(\bar C=\varnothing\).

We first prove invariance along the role-state graph.  At its root \(\rho_0=(X,C)\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}query}\) gives
\[
 K_{\rho_0,\mathbf M}(y)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{3}
\]
Consider an edge that moves a nonempty current bucket intersection \(T\subseteq\bar X\) from treatment to conditioning.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\) includes this edge only when the corresponding Rule--2 separation holds.  Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}selected\text{-}rule\text{-}two}\) with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X\setminus T.
\]
These four sets are pairwise disjoint by the role partition and \(Y\cap W=\varnothing\).  Using the restrictions of \(a\) on both sides of the Rule--2 equality yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid \bar C=\bar c,
 \operatorname{do}(T=a_T,\bar X\setminus T=a_{\bar X\setminus T}),
 S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid T=a_T,\bar C=\bar c,
 \operatorname{do}(\bar X\setminus T=a_{\bar X\setminus T}),
 S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=K_{(\bar X\setminus T,\,\bar C\cup T),\mathbf M}(y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
If instead an edge moves a nonempty \(T\subseteq\bar C\) from conditioning to treatment, apply the same lemma with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C\setminus T,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X.
\]
Reading its equality from right to left gives
\[
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 =K_{(\bar X\cup T,\,\bar C\setminus T),\mathbf M}(y).
 \tag{5}
\]
Induction on the finite length of any directed trace from \(\rho_0\), using (3)--(5), proves
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)=\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)
 \quad\text{for every reachable role state }\rho.
 \tag{6}
\]

Suppose now that Branch-sCIDP succeeds at \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\).  Its terminal sIDP call has outcome set \(A_0=Y\cup\bar C\) and intervention set \(B_0=\bar X\).  They are disjoint, and \(A_0\neq\varnothing\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}nonempty\text{-}outcome}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}soundness}\), applied directly on the published positive discrete class \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\), therefore gives, pointwise for every \(y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)\),
\[
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x).
 \tag{7}
\]
This is not an inference from the rational binary certificate subclass.  Summing (7) over the full finite outcome support and using the definition of \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 &=\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x)\\
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 \bar C=\bar c\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)>0,
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
where the last inequality follows from (2) and the positive selected-intervention normalizer.  Dividing (7) by (8), applying the definition of conditional probability, and then applying (6), we obtain
\[
 \frac{F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 {\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 =K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus the normalized returned expression is an observed-law identifying map for the causal target.  Its equality with the target has been derived from Rule--2 invariance and sIDP soundness, rather than imposed by definition.

It remains to prove the finite-search and cache bounds.  A role state is uniquely determined by \(\bar X\subseteq W\), since \(\bar C=W\setminus\bar X\).  Hence
\[
 |\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)|\leq 2^{|W|}=2^{|X\cup C|}.
 \tag{10}
\]
A trace with no repeated state and \(r\) visited states has \(r-1\) edges, so (10) gives the asserted upper bound \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\) on its length.

At each visited state, the outer enumeration tests at most two directions for each of at most \(n\) buckets.  Each relevant manipulated graph has polynomial size in \(n\).  A Rule--2 separation test is decided by a finite reachability search over its admissible edge-incidence states; bucket formation, anterior closure, and region formation are also graph searches of polynomial size.  Consequently all outer role-state work is
\[
 O\!\left(2^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{11}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}recursion\text{-}structure}\), a deterministic BuildTree subproblem is keyed by one region \(R\subseteq V\), and a fixing subproblem is keyed by one pair \(R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\).  There are \(2^n\) keys of the first kind and
\[
 \#\{(R,T_0):R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\}
 =\sum_{T_0\subseteq V}2^{|T_0|}
 =(1+2)^n=3^n
 \tag{12}
\]
keys of the second kind.  The final equality follows directly by assigning each vertex independently to \(R\), to \(T_0\setminus R\), or to \(V\setminus T_0\).  The same recursion lemma states that BuildTree descends only to proper region children and that every successful fixing iteration removes a nonempty bucket.  Therefore each deterministic key terminates.  Under Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}shared\text{-}formula\text{-}cache}\), it is evaluated at most once and incurs only \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) graph work.  Equations (11) and (12) thus bound all cached graph computation by
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{13}
\]
Each marginalization, product, quotient, and assembly operation contributes a constant-arity node to the shared formula DAG.  Constructing and emitting those nodes costs \(O(L_{\mathrm{form}})\) by the definition of \(L_{\mathrm{form}}\).  Combining this output cost with (13) proves
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}}\right).
\]
The proof invoked sIDP soundness only after a terminal call succeeded.  It therefore gives no implication from \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) to nonidentification, exactly as claimed.

Assume \(S=\varnothing\).  The selection event is then the sure event, so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}query}\) reduces to
\[
 \psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c).
 \tag{1}
\]
In this specialization, \(\mathrm{lem{:}selected\text{-}rule\text{-}two}\) is the ordinary PAG Rule--2 equality because no selection coordinate occurs on either side.

Suppose first that CIDP succeeds.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\), it performs a finite sequence of legal Rule--2 moves of nonempty intersections with current buckets, reaches a role state \(\rho_\star=(\bar X_\star,\bar C_\star)\), and identifies the joint kernel
\[
 P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y,\bar C_\star\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X_\star)
 \right).
 \tag{2}
\]
Every move in this sequence satisfies exactly the edge condition in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\).  Hence \(\rho_\star\in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\), and Branch-sCIDP visits it unless an earlier terminal call succeeds.  If sIDP returned \(\operatorname{Fail}\) at \(\rho_\star\), Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}completeness}\) would imply that the joint kernel (2) is not identified over the represented model class.  This contradicts the identification of (2) supplied by the CIDP contract.  Therefore sIDP succeeds at \(\rho_\star\), or Branch-sCIDP has already succeeded at an earlier visited state.  Thus CIDP success implies Branch-sCIDP success.

Conversely, suppose Branch-sCIDP succeeds.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}branch\text{-}soundness}\) supplies an observed-law functional equal, throughout the represented positive discrete class, to the right-hand side of (1).  The conditional causal query is therefore identified.  Completeness in \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\) rules out CIDP failure, so CIDP succeeds.  This proves agreement of the two identification decisions.

For the formula claim, let \(\Phi_{\mathrm B}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) denote any normalized functional returned by a successful Branch-sCIDP state, and let \(\Phi_{\mathrm C}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) denote the normalized joint functional returned by CIDP.  Branch soundness and the soundness clause of \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\), respectively, imply that for every compatible positive discrete model \(\mathbf M\),
\[
 \Phi_{\mathrm B}(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c)
 =\Phi_{\mathrm C}(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M}).
 \tag{3}
\]
Both normalizations are defined because the positive discrete model assumption makes their conditioning denominators positive; finite marginalization covers the cases \(C=\varnothing\) or an empty terminal conditioning role.  Equation (3) shows pointwise equality on the observational-law domain represented by \(\mathcal P\).  Hence every successful Branch-sCIDP formula is algebraically equivalent, as an identifying functional on that domain, to a CIDP identifying functional.

Fix a family satisfying \texttt{def:affine-mechanism-family} and \texttt{def:affine-rank-system}, together with the represented graph, forest, and legal-role-trace scaffold required by \texttt{def:locked-certificate}; write its reachable terminal role state as \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\).  Let the assignment of every state be the restriction of the fixed assignment \((x,c)\) to its current treatment and conditioning roles.  By \texttt{def:rational-binary-class}, \texttt{ass:binary-certificate-support}, and \texttt{ass:rational-interior-mechanisms}, \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\) has finite binary state spaces and rational local stochastic-mechanism entries strictly between zero and one.  Exactly one normalized local table is changed from \(\theta\) to \(\theta+t v\), where \(v=R_Tq\in T\); all other mechanisms and all structural incidences are held fixed.

We first prove the exact affine identities used by the rank test.  Fix either the observational regime or the terminal regime \(\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x)\), and fix a complete assignment \(\omega\) of all nonintervened endogenous and latent variables.  In the truncated finite factorization, the varied local table occurs at most once.  If it occurs, for a coordinate \(j(\omega)\) its contribution gives
\[
 p_t(\omega)
 =\bigl(\theta_{j(\omega)}+t v_{j(\omega)}\bigr)
   \prod_{\ell\ne j(\omega)}p_\ell(\omega)
 =p_0(\omega)+t\dot p_v(\omega);
\]
if the variable governed by that table is intervened upon, the factor is removed and \(p_t(\omega)=p_0(\omega)\).  All marginalizations are finite sums.  Hence, with rational coefficients linear in \(v\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 o_z(t)&=o_z(0)+t\dot o_z(v),&
 Z_o(t)&=Z_o(0)+t\dot Z_o(v),\\
 h(t)&=h(0)+t\dot h(v),&
 k(t)&=k(0)+t\dot k(v),&
 Z_x(t)&=Z_x(0)+t\dot Z_x(v).
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{1}
\]
Thus affinity is a consequence of varying one local factor, rather than an approximation.  Strict positivity of all base mechanisms and nonemptiness of the finite assignment spaces imply
\[
 Z_o(0)>0,\qquad Z_x(0)>0,\qquad h(0)>0.                         \tag{2}
\]
Indeed, each quantity in (2) is a finite sum containing a strictly positive complete-assignment mass; for \(h(0)\), the fixed assignment \(\bar C=\bar c\) is in the binary support.  The same argument applies at every sufficiently small perturbation that keeps every mechanism entry positive.

By the definitions of the selected observational law, the terminal joint kernel, the denominator, and the numerator,
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M(t)}(z)=\frac{o_z(t)}{Z_o(t)},\qquad
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}(\bar c;\bar x)=\frac{h(t)}{Z_x(t)},\qquad
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}(y,\bar c;\bar x)=\frac{k(t)}{Z_x(t)}.    \tag{3}
\]
For every positive perturbation model, substituting (1) and cross-multiplying in (3) gives the exact identities
\[
 \frac{o_z(t)}{Z_o(t)}-\frac{o_z(0)}{Z_o(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_o(0)\dot o_z(v)-o_z(0)\dot Z_o(v)\}}
        {Z_o(t)Z_o(0)},                                          \tag{4}
\]
\[
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-D_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot h(v)-h(0)\dot Z_x(v)\}}
        {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)},                                          \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-N_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot k(v)-k(0)\dot Z_x(v)\}}
        {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)}.                                          \tag{6}
\]
The products of the two slopes cancel in each subtraction, so (4)--(6) hold for finite \(t\), not merely to first order.  By \texttt{def:affine-rank-system}, after \(v=R_Tq\) the braces in (4), over all observed cells \(z\), followed by the brace in (5), are precisely the coordinates of \(E_Tq\); the brace in (6) is \(b_Tq\).

We next prove the rank equivalence over \(\mathbb Q\).  If \(b_T\) lies in the rational row space of \(E_T\), then \(b_Tq=0\) for every \(q\in\ker(E_T)\).  Conversely, suppose \(b_Tq=0\) for every \(q\in\ker(E_T)\).  The prescription
\[
 \ell(E_Tq)=b_Tq                                                \tag{7}
\]
is then a well-defined rational linear functional on \(\operatorname{im}(E_T)\): two preimages differ by a vector in \(\ker(E_T)\).  Extend a rational basis of \(\operatorname{im}(E_T)\) to a rational basis of the codomain and extend \(\ell\) to the added basis vectors.  Equation (7) then says \(b_T=\ell E_T\), so \(b_T\) is in the row space of \(E_T\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\exists q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}:\ E_Tq=0\ \text{and}\ b_Tq\ne0\\
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow b_T\notin\operatorname{row}(E_T)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \operatorname{rank}\!\begin{bmatrix}E_T\\ b_T\end{bmatrix}
 >\operatorname{rank}(E_T).                                    \tag{8}
\end{aligned}
\]
Rational row reduction decides (8) and, in the strict-rank case, returns a rational null vector \(q\) with \(b_Tq\ne0\).

The condition is independent of the rational basis used for \(T\).  If \(R_T'\) is another basis matrix, there is an invertible rational matrix \(H\) with \(R_T'=R_TH\).  Consequently
\[
 ER_T'=E_TH,\qquad bR_T'=b_TH.                                  \tag{9}
\]
Right multiplication by \(H\) preserves both ranks in (8), while \(q'=H^{-1}q\) preserves the mechanism direction because \(R_T'q'=R_Tq\).  This proves basis independence.

Assume henceforth that (8) holds, use the returned \(q\), and put \(v=R_Tq\).  Since \(b_Tq=bv\ne0\), one has \(v\ne0\).  Define
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{pos}}
 =\frac12\min_{j:v_j\ne0}
 \left\{\frac{\theta_j}{|v_j|},
             \frac{1-\theta_j}{|v_j|}\right\}.                 \tag{10}
\]
This is a positive rational number.  Because \(v\in T\), its coordinates sum to zero separately in every probability block.  Hence \(\theta+t v\) remains normalized, and (10) implies \(0<\theta_j+t v_j<1\) for every coordinate whenever \(|t|<\delta_{\mathrm{pos}}\).

We now verify represented-class membership rather than inferring it from positivity.  The affine-family definition fixes the parent domains, directed and latent incidences, selection vertices, state spaces, and all unvaried mechanisms; changing entries of the same indexed local table therefore introduces no forbidden parent or latent incidence.  Under the structural representation convention this already leaves the represented \(\mathcal G\), and hence \(\mathcal M\in[\mathcal P]_{\mathsf M}\), unchanged.  If the representation records only active displayed parent incidences, let \(\mathcal A\) be the finite set of incidences whose activity must be retained in the varied table.  Since the base SCM realizes \(\mathcal G\), for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) there are two table coordinates \(j_a,j_a'\), differing only in that parent's value with all other arguments and the child value fixed, such that
\[
 \alpha_a=\theta_{j_a}-\theta_{j_a'}\ne0.
\]
Put \(\beta_a=v_{j_a}-v_{j_a'}\) and set
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{rep}}
 =\begin{cases}
 1,&\text{if }\beta_a=0\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A,\\[2mm]
 \displaystyle\min\!\left\{1,
   \frac12\min_{a:\beta_a\ne0}\frac{|\alpha_a|}{|\beta_a|}\right\},
 &\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}                                                    \tag{11}
\]
For \(|t|<\delta_{\mathrm{rep}}\), each chosen activity contrast obeys
\[
 |\alpha_a+t\beta_a|
 \ge |\alpha_a|-|t|\,|\beta_a|>\frac12|\alpha_a|>0             \tag{12}
\]
when \(\beta_a\ne0\), and it is unchanged when \(\beta_a=0\).  Thus every required active incidence remains active.  In either representation convention, (11)--(12), together with the unchanged structural and latent incidences, prove that all sufficiently small perturbations remain in the same represented realization.

Set
\[
 \delta=\min\{\delta_{\mathrm{pos}},\delta_{\mathrm{rep}}\}.   \tag{13}
\]
Equations (10)--(13) make \(\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) exactly computable.  For every rational \(t\) satisfying \(0<|t|<\delta\), the changed table is rational, normalized, and strictly positive; every other mechanism is unchanged; binary support and the represented realization are preserved.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbf M(0),\mathbf M(t)
 \in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P)
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P).                          \tag{14}
\]

Take \(\mathbf M_0=\mathbf M(0)\) and \(\mathbf M_1=\mathbf M(t)\).  Positivity from (14) makes every denominator in (4)--(6) nonzero.  Since \(E_Tq=0\), equations (4)--(5) yield, for all full observed cells \(z\),
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_0}(z)=P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_1}(z),
 \qquad
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(\bar c;\bar x)
 =D_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(\bar c;\bar x)>0.                       \tag{15}
\]
Thus the complete normalized selected observational laws, not merely selected unnormalized masses, agree.  Since \(b_Tq\ne0\) and \(t\ne0\), equation (6) gives
\[
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(y,\bar c;\bar x)
 \ne N_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(y,\bar c;\bar x).                   \tag{16}
\]
Consequently, by (3) and the locked positive denominator in (15), the two terminal selected conditional kernels differ:
\[
 \frac{N_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(y,\bar c;\bar x)}
      {D_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(\bar c;\bar x)}
 \ne
 \frac{N_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(y,\bar c;\bar x)}
      {D_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(\bar c;\bar x)}.                   \tag{17}
\]

It remains to transfer (17) along the legal role trace.  By \texttt{def:reachable-role-graph}, the trace starts at \(\rho_0=(X,C)\), ends at \(\rho\), and every edge moves a nonempty current bucket intersection whose corresponding Rule--2 separation holds.  Apply \texttt{lem:selected-rule-two} at an edge with \(A_0=Y\), with \(B_0\) equal to the moved intersection, and with the other action and conditioning coordinates supplied by the two adjacent role states.  Its disjointness conditions follow from the role partition and \texttt{ass:disjoint-query-sets}; its positivity condition follows from (14).  The lemma identifies the two adjacent conditional kernels, with the displayed equality read in the reverse direction for a reverse move.  Induction over the finite trace gives, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \frac{N_{\rho,\mathbf M_j}(y,\bar c;\bar x)}
      {D_{\rho,\mathbf M_j}(\bar c;\bar x)}
 =P_{\mathbf M_j}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M_j}(y;x,c).                                   \tag{18}
\]
Equations (15)--(18) exhibit two models with the same \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) but different \(\psi\).  By \texttt{def:identification} and the inclusion in (14), this pair certifies nonidentification over the published positive discrete class.  This is a negative transfer from the rational binary subclass; no positive completeness conclusion for that subclass or the published class is used.  The represented graph, nested forests, legal trace, models, and exact tables are precisely the remaining data required by \texttt{def:locked-certificate}, so \(\operatorname{LockCompile}\) returns the claimed \(\Gamma\).

Finally, we establish the two bit-complexity claims in the stated encodings.  Clear the encoded rational denominators in \(E_T\) and \(b_T\) and perform pivoted fraction-free elimination.  At an elimination step with nonzero pivots, update an uneliminated entry by
\[
 a_{ij}^{(r+1)}
 =\frac{a_{rr}^{(r)}a_{ij}^{(r)}-a_{ir}^{(r)}a_{rj}^{(r)}}
        {a_{r-1,r-1}^{(r-1)}},                                 \tag{19}
\]
with the initial previous pivot equal to one; row or column permutations supply a nonzero pivot whenever one exists.  Expanding the two products in the numerator of (19) and grouping permutations according to whether they use the pivot position shows that the numerator is the previous pivot times the corresponding next-order minor.  Induction on \(r\) therefore proves both that every division in (19) is exact and that every stored nonzero value is, up to sign, a minor of the integerized input matrix.  If that matrix has dimensions at most \(s\) and entries of bit length at most \(B\), the Leibniz expansion bounds the absolute value of an \(r\)-by-\(r\) minor by \(r!2^{rB}\), hence bounds its bit length by
\[
 rB+\lceil\log_2(r!)\rceil+1
 =O\!\left(s(B+\log s)\right).                                 \tag{20}
\]
There are polynomially many updates, and (20) bounds all intermediate bit lengths polynomially in the matrix encoding.  Back-substitution uses only a polynomial number of operations on these minors and returns a rational null vector.  Thus the two ranks, a rational null vector \(q\), the activity witnesses, \(\delta\), and a valid choice such as \(t=\delta/2\) are computable in \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}})\) bit operations.

The compiler next copies the supplied graph, role trace, and forest objects and expands the two rational SCM evaluations.  Each complete-assignment atom is a finite product of encoded local probabilities, and every displayed marginal is a finite exact sum of such atoms.  The dense atoms and the arithmetic trace are included in the expanded output measured by \(L_{\Gamma}\); sequential products and sums have numerator and denominator bit lengths at most polynomial in the total input-plus-output bit length.  It follows that construction and writing of the complete certificate take
\[
 \operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}}+L_{\Gamma})
\]
bit operations.

For verification, acyclicity, ancestry, latent projection, endpoint compatibility, legality of every role edge, and the rooted nested-forest predicates reduce to finitely many adjacency scans and directed-reachability searches, each polynomial in the displayed graph size.  If representation is checked through the full separation model instead, exhaustive comparison is still polynomial in the expanded encoding: there are at most \(4^n\) disjoint vertex triples, while the dense observed table contained in \(\Gamma\) has at least \(2^n\) cells, so \(4^n\le L_{\Gamma}^2\).  The verifier also checks every rational probability block for exact normalization and strict positivity, checks the retained activity contrasts from (12), recomputes the displayed observational and interventional atoms from the dense factorization and arithmetic trace, and checks (15)--(16) by exact cross-multiplication.  The number of entries and the bit length of every operand are bounded by \(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma}\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Verify}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C,\Gamma)
 \quad\text{runs in}\quad
 \operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma})
\]
bit operations.  This proves every assertion of the theorem.

All variables in the informative-lock template are binary.  The displayed local success probabilities and their Bernoulli complements belong to
\[
 \left\{\frac14,\frac12,\frac34,
              \frac5{16},\frac7{16},\frac9{16},\frac{11}{16}\right\}.
\]
Thus every local-table entry is rational and strictly between zero and one, as required by \(\text{ass:rational-interior-mechanisms}\), and binary support is supplied by \(\text{ass:binary-certificate-support}\).  The conditional law of \(X_i\) changes with \(U_i\).  For either sign \(\sigma\), the conditional law of \(Y_i\) changes with each of \(X_i\) and \(U_i\).  The conditional law of \(C_i\) changes with \(Y_i\), and that of \(S_i\) changes with each of \(Y_i\) and \(C_i\).  Consequently every displayed parent is active, and the induced directed graph is exactly \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\).

We next check the two projections in the informative graph-certificate definition.  Marginalizing \(U_i\) preserves \(X_i\to Y_i\) and induces \(X_i\leftrightarrow Y_i\) from \(X_i\leftarrow U_i\to Y_i\); the arrows \(Y_i\to C_i\), \(Y_i\to S_i\), and \(C_i\to S_i\) remain.  Every other path between nonadjacent vertices has an observed internal vertex, and hence creates no additional latent-projection edge.  The selected acyclic directed mixed graph is therefore precisely \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\).

For the selected latent projection onto \(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}\), all three observed vertices are ancestors of \(S_i\), so the endpoint marks on the adjacencies \(X_i-Y_i\) and \(Y_i-C_i\) are tails.  There is no \(X_i-C_i\) adjacency: in the relevant ancestral moral graph, after conditioning on and removing \(Y_i\) and \(S_i\), the vertex \(C_i\) is disconnected from the component containing \(X_i\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i.                 \tag{1}
\]
The three-vertex noncollider chain has no invariant endpoint mark in its input-free equivalence class, so its completed partial graph is
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}
 =X_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}Y_i
       \mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}C_i.
\]
These direct projection and equivalence-class checks give
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}),
 \qquad \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M},
 \qquad \mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}. \tag{2}
\]
Combining binary support, strict rational positivity, (2), and \(\text{def:rational-binary-class}\) yields
\[
 \mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+},\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}
 \in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}). \tag{3}
\]

We now compute the observational and interventional laws.  Since \(P(U_i=1)=1/2\), the denominators below are \(P(X_i=a)=1/2>0\), and Bayes' rule gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(X_i=1)&=\tfrac12\tfrac14+\tfrac12\tfrac34=\tfrac12,
 &P(U_i=1\mid X_i=1)&=\frac{(1/2)(3/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac34=r_1,\\
 P(X_i=0)&=\tfrac12\tfrac34+\tfrac12\tfrac14=\tfrac12,
 &P(U_i=1\mid X_i=0)&=\frac{(1/2)(1/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac14=r_0.
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{4}
\]
For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the law of total probability and the outcome table in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
   \left\{\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}(u-r_a)\right\}
   P(U_i=u\mid X_i=a)\\
 &=\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}
   \{P(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)-r_a\}=\frac12,                 \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality uses (4).  Hence both signs have the same unselected observed law and
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b)=\frac14
 \quad\text{for every }a,b\in\{0,1\}.                  \tag{6}
\]
Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), SCM modularity removes the local factor for \(X_i\) and leaves \(U_i\) fair.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_+(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12+\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac9{16},\\
 P_-(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12-\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac7{16}. \tag{7}
\end{aligned}
\]

The appended \(C_i,S_i\) tables instantiate \(\text{lem:selection-equalizer-lift}\).  Namely, set
\[
 g_b(d):=P(C_i=d\mid Y_i=b),
 \qquad \lambda_0=\lambda_1:=\frac3{16},
 \qquad \Lambda:=\lambda_0+\lambda_1=\frac38.          \tag{8}
\]
For every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\), direct multiplication gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
 (b,d)&(0,0)&(0,1)&(1,0)&(1,1)\\ \hline
 g_b(d)P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=b,C_i=d)
 &(3/4)(1/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(3/4)(1/4)
\end{array}
=\frac3{16}.                                             \tag{9}
\]
Moreover \(0<3/16<1/4=\min_b g_b(d)\) for both \(d\), so every positivity premise of that lemma holds.  Both appended parent relations are active, as checked above, so its graph qualification holds as well.  Applying its observational identity to (6) yields
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)
 =\frac14\frac3{16}=\frac3{64}.                         \tag{10}
\]
There are eight observed cells; summing (10) gives \(P_\sigma(S_i=1)=3/8>0\).  Division by this normalizer gives
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d\mid S_i=1)
 =\frac{3/64}{3/8}=\frac18.                              \tag{11}
\]
Thus the two complete selected observational laws coincide and have full support.

The interventional identities in \(\text{lem:selection-equalizer-lift}\), together with (7)--(8), give the common terminal selection normalizer \(3/8\) and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},\sigma}}(1;0)
 &=\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac12,\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac9{16}\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac9{32},\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac7{16}\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac7{32}.    \tag{12}
\end{aligned}
\]
The common conditioning denominator in (12) is strictly positive.  Dividing each numerator by it gives conditional causal effects \(9/16\) and \(7/16\), respectively.  The common \(C_i\) table also gives
\[
 P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=\frac34\ne\frac14
 =P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0),                                   \tag{13}
\]
so the connected conditioning vertex is informative before selection.

It remains to verify the terminal forest assertions in \(\text{def:informative-graph-certificate}\).  The graph \(F_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is bidirected-connected, every vertex has at most one directed child, and its unique childless root is \(Y_i\).  The singleton \(F'_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is a proper C-subforest with the same root.  Also
\[
 V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\},
 \qquad
 V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing.          \tag{14}
\]
After intervention on \(X_i\), the root \(Y_i\) belongs to the terminal set and has directed paths to \(C_i\) and \(S_i\).  Hence
\[
 R_{\mathrm{inf}}=\{Y_i\}
 \subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}
 (\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\}).                                     \tag{15}
\]
For the maximal selection-exchange coordinate, \(S=\{S_i\}\), so the only nonempty candidate is \(D=\{S_i\}\).  In the corresponding input-augmented graph, the path
\[
 I_{S_i}\longrightarrow S_i\longleftarrow C_i           \tag{16}
\]
is open when conditioning on \(S_i\): its only internal vertex is a conditioned collider, and it has no noncollider at which the path could be blocked.  Thus \(I_{S_i}\) and \(C_i\) fail the required id-separation, making \(\{S_i\}\) inadmissible.  The empty set is admissible vacuously and is the only remaining subset.  Consequently
\[
 D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing.                     \tag{17}
\]
The bidirected-connectivity, common-root, treatment-intersection, ancestry, and maximal-exchange checks (14)--(17) are exactly the terminal selected-hedge predicates named in the informative graph-certificate definition.  Thus \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) is the asserted terminal selected hedge for \((\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\},\{X_i\})\).

Finally, consider the same-graph alternative \(\widetilde P\) from \(\text{sym:Alt}\), obtained by changing only \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) from \(1/4\) to \(1/2\).  The altered success probability and its complement are strictly positive rational numbers.  At fixed \(C_i=0\), the selection table still changes with \(Y_i\), and at fixed \(Y_i=0\), it still changes with \(C_i\); hence both arrows into \(S_i\) remain active and the represented graph is unchanged.  Equations (4)--(6) are unaffected, so the two signs retain the same unselected observed law.  Their \(C_i\) and modified \(S_i\) mechanisms are common; factorization therefore gives equal unnormalized selected observational masses cell by cell, and normalization gives equal full selected observational laws.

Put \(p=P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))\).  When \(Y_i=0\), summing the two unchanged products in (9) gives \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=0)=3/8\).  When \(Y_i=1\), the \(C_i=0\) product remains \(3/16\), whereas the modified \(C_i=1\) product is \((3/4)(1/2)=3/8\); hence \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=9/16\).  It follows by the law of total probability that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde P(S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac38+p\frac9{16}=\frac{6+3p}{16},\\
 \widetilde P(C_i=1,S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac3{16}+p\frac38=\frac{3+3p}{16}.            \tag{18}
\end{aligned}
\]
The first quantity in (18) is positive.  Therefore the modified selected conditioning denominator is
\[
 \widetilde D_\sigma(1;0)
 =\frac{3+3p}{6+3p}=\frac{1+p}{2+p}.                    \tag{19}
\]
Substituting \(p=9/16\) and \(p=7/16\) from (7) gives
\[
 \widetilde D_+=\frac{25}{41},
 \qquad
 \widetilde D_-=\frac{23}{39}.                         \tag{20}
\]
These fractions differ because \(25\cdot39=975\ne943=23\cdot41\).  Hence equality of the denominators in (12) is the tuned informative cancellation supplied by (8)--(9), rather than a structural consequence of the represented graph.  This proves every assertion of the proposition.

Fix \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\) and \(a,d\in\{0,1\}\). By the SCM factorization for \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{iso}}\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}isolated\mbox{-}bow\mbox{-}template}\),
\[
 P_{\sigma}(u,x,y,c,s)
 =P(u)P(c)P(x\mid u)P_{\sigma}(y\mid x,u)P(s\mid y).
\]
All displayed local probabilities in that definition are rational and lie strictly between zero and one. In particular, the four possible outcome-mechanism values belong to
\[
 \left\{\frac{5}{16},\frac{7}{16},\frac{9}{16},\frac{11}{16}\right\}.
\]
Thus every cell needed below is positive, all subsequent conditioning operations have positive denominators, and, together with Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}binary\mbox{-}certificate\mbox{-}support}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}rational\mbox{-}interior\mbox{-}mechanisms}\), both sign-indexed models have the stipulated positive rational binary support.

The treatment marginal is fair:
\[
 P(X_b=1)
 =\frac12\frac14+\frac12\frac34
 =\frac12,
 \qquad
 P(X_b=0)
 =\frac12\frac34+\frac12\frac14
 =\frac12.
\]
Bayes' formula therefore applies with a positive denominator and gives
\[
 P(U_b=1\mid X_b=0)
 =\frac{(1/2)(1/4)}{1/2}
 =\frac14=r_0^b,
 \qquad
 P(U_b=1\mid X_b=1)
 =\frac{(1/2)(3/4)}{1/2}
 =\frac34=r_1^b.
\]
Consequently, by the outcome mechanism in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}isolated\mbox{-}bow\mbox{-}template}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1\mid X_b=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left\{\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}(u-r_a^b)\right\}
 P(U_b=u\mid X_b=a)\\
 &=\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}
 \left\{P(U_b=1\mid X_b=a)-r_a^b\right\}\\
 &=\frac12.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(C_b\) is an isolated fair root in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{iso}}\), the factorization gives \(P(C_b=d)=1/2\) and makes \(C_b\) independent of \((X_b,Y_b,S_b)\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=1,S_b=1)
 &=P(X_b=a)P(C_b=d)
   P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1\mid X_b=a)P(S_b=1\mid Y_b=1)\\
 &=\frac12\frac12\frac12\frac23
 =\frac1{12},\\
 P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=0,S_b=1)
 &=P(X_b=a)P(C_b=d)
   P_{\sigma}(Y_b=0\mid X_b=a)P(S_b=1\mid Y_b=0)\\
 &=\frac12\frac12\frac12\frac13
 =\frac1{24}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Summing these cells over the two values of \(a\) and the two values of \(d\) yields
\[
 P_{\sigma}(S_b=1)
 =4\left(\frac1{12}+\frac1{24}\right)
 =\frac12.
\]
It follows cell by cell that
\[
 P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=y\mid S_b=1)
 =
 \begin{cases}
  1/6,&y=1,\\
  1/12,&y=0,
 \end{cases}
\]
which is independent of \(\sigma\). Since the binary cells indexed by \((a,d,y)\) exhaust the observed sample space, the two full selected observational laws agree.

Now intervene to set \(X_b=0\). The truncated SCM factorization leaves the fair root \(U_b\) unchanged. Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
 p_{\sigma}
 &:=P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))\\
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left\{\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}\left(u-\frac14\right)\right\}P(U_b=u)\\
 &=\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)
 =\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{16}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
 p_{+}=\frac9{16},
 \qquad
 p_{-}=\frac7{16}.
\]
The selection mechanism depends only on \(Y_b\), so its postintervention normalizer is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Z_{\sigma}
 &:=P_{\sigma}(S_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))\\
 &=\frac23p_{\sigma}+\frac13(1-p_{\sigma})
 =\frac{1+p_{\sigma}}3.
\end{aligned}
\]
It follows that
\[
 Z_{+}=\frac{25}{48},
 \qquad
 Z_{-}=\frac{23}{48},
\]
both of which are positive. Take the terminal role state with \(\bar X=\{X_b\}\), \(\bar C=\{C_b\}\), outcome \(Y_b\), and assignments \(\bar x=0\), \(\bar c=1\). Isolation of \(C_b\) is preserved by the intervention, and hence the selected terminal joint kernel is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\sigma}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac{P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1,C_b=1,S_b=1
       \mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))}{Z_{\sigma}}\\
 &=\frac{p_{\sigma}(1/2)(2/3)}{Z_{\sigma}}
 =\frac{p_{\sigma}}{1+p_{\sigma}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Substitution gives the two claimed joint numerators,
\[
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},+}}(1,1;0)=\frac9{25},
 \qquad
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},-}}(1,1;0)=\frac7{23}.
\]
Moreover, Definition \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\sigma}}(1;0)=\sum_{y'\in\{0,1\}}J_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\sigma}}(y',1;0)\), followed by the same isolation factorization, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\sigma}}(1;0)
 &=P_{\sigma}(C_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0),S_b=1)\\
 &=\frac{P(C_b=1)P_{\sigma}(S_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))}{Z_{\sigma}}\\
 &=\frac{(1/2)Z_{\sigma}}{Z_{\sigma}}
 =\frac12.
\end{aligned}
\]
The division is valid because \(Z_{\sigma}>0\). Normalizing the selected joint kernel by this denominator therefore yields
\[
 P_{\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},+}}(Y_b=1\mid
 \operatorname{do}(X_b=0),C_b=1,S_b=1)
 =\frac{9/25}{1/2}=\frac{18}{25},
\]
and
\[
 P_{\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},-}}(Y_b=1\mid
 \operatorname{do}(X_b=0),C_b=1,S_b=1)
 =\frac{7/23}{1/2}=\frac{14}{23}.
\]
Finally, the identity \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\sigma}}(1;0)=1/2\) used only that \(C_b\) is an isolated fair root; it did not use cancellation between the sign-indexed outcome mechanisms. Thus denominator equality is structurally automatic in this baseline, establishing precisely why the example is vacuous as evidence for generic denominator locking.
